findings.issue: PaymentFeignClient uses only InternalFeignConfig, not NoUserTokenFeignConfig, so the global CorrelationAndAuthForwardingInterceptor copies the caller's bearer onto any call made from a request thread. In PR-A, ensureRow is called only from the @Scheduled relay, which has no request context, so no bearer is sent. The inline createPayment at placement already forwards the customer's bearer to /internal/payments. That was true before this PR and the target is in-cluster only. PR-B plans to run the ensure inside admin refund and collect requests, where an admin bearer would be forwarded.
findings.fix: Add NoUserTokenFeignConfig to the PaymentFeignClient configuration (as CartInternalFeignClient does), in PR-B at the latest, and add a test that ensureRow and create send X-Internal-Token and no Authorization header when a request context is bound.

findings.issue: The 60-second REPAIR_DELAY only assumes placement finishes within 60 seconds. Placement makes several remote calls between the save and createPayment (reserve stock, deals, exchange, coupon, coins, wallet debit). If they are slow, the relay can run the ensure first. It then creates and attaches a COD_PENDING row, and placement may later abandon or unwind the order to CANCELLED. The ensure also has a gap between checking the cancelled status and attaching the row. Either way a cancelled order can be left with a COD_PENDING row. No money moves: COD create debits nothing, cancelUnpaid keeps COD_PENDING, and COD_PENDING routes to no refund. Both paths still converge on the single row that payment-service keeps per order_id.
findings.fix: Accept, and record the case in the runbook. Optionally have the ensure re-check the order status after the attach, or tie REPAIR_DELAY to the sum of the placement Feign timeouts.

findings.issue: The runbook says a WARN "already has a ... payment row" marks a non-COD row, but CodPaymentRows logs this case at ERROR. An operator grepping or alerting on WARN will miss it.
findings.fix: Change the runbook to say ERROR, or log at WARN, so the two match.

findings.issue: In the bad-data case (a COD order whose order id already has a Razorpay CARD row that is REQUIRES_PAYMENT with no provider order), payment-service create sends the ensure into awaitRazorpayOrder. If that row's lease has run out, the ensure can take over and create a Razorpay order (a provider call, not a charge) before CONFLICT_METHOD is returned. No money moves and nothing is attached.
findings.fix: Accept as bad-data only, or in PR-B let payment-service create return an existing row without the Razorpay wait when the request method is COD and the row's method is not.

summary: I found no blocker or major issue in PR-A's money path. The ensure cannot make a second row: payment-service create is idempotent on the order_id unique index, and the new concurrency test runs 8 threads and checks that one row exists, no wallet transaction is written and Razorpay is never called. The COD create path makes no wallet debit or provider call. A CARD row or any non-COD row is never converted or attached (CONFLICT_METHOD, and the row goes DONE). The payment_id is attached only through a conditional JPQL update (where paymentId is null), and the inline attach writes the same id payment-service returns for that order_id, so a relay racing the inline create, or two relays (under JobLock), converge on one row and one id. The amount matches placement: totalAmount minus walletAmount read from the saved order, and the order's wallet part is set before the save; zero or negative remainders are skipped. The relay runs with no request context, so ensureRow carries only X-Internal-Token and no user bearer. The outbox payload is only the order id. last_error holds e.toString() as before, and the logs carry order id, payment id, method and amounts, with no user id, email or address. The repair row sits on its own synthetic aggregate and is enqueued in the same transaction as the order's saveAndFlush, so a failed insert rolls back the order. An old build filters kinds with IN (:known), so the row is reported and left PENDING with no side effects and holds back no other aggregate. The new SQL and JPQL bind every value as a parameter, including make_interval secs, so there is no injection. No new endpoint and no new dependency are added. The minor findings are: the payment Feign client should strip the forwarded bearer before PR-B calls it from request threads; the 60-second delay can let the ensure leave a harmless COD_PENDING row on an order that is cancelled later; the runbook says WARN where the code logs ERROR; and in a bad-data case the ensure can trigger a Razorpay order creation (no charge).
